items.definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience, or an official organization with such power.
exampleSentences: The mayor lacked the authority to overturn the council's decision.
Local authorities issued an evacuation order ahead of the storm.
Her long experience in constitutional law gave her considerable authority on the subject.

items.definition: A particular part of a place, subject, or activity, or a region defined by administrative or geographic boundaries.
exampleSentences: The new zoning law restricts construction in residential areas.
Human rights has become a central area of international policy.
Local officials designated the flood-prone area a disaster zone.

items.definition: To form or make up a whole, or to establish something formally, especially a legal or official body.
exampleSentences: Ethnic minorities constitute nearly twenty percent of the country's population.
The treaty constitutes a legally binding agreement between the two states.
Parliament voted to constitute a special commission to investigate the allegations.
items.translationTR: oluşturmak, meydana getirmek; (resmi olarak) kurmak, teşkil etmek

items.definition: The natural world of land, air, and water, or the surrounding conditions, circumstances, and influences affecting a person, group, or activity.
exampleSentences: The new regulations aim to protect the environment from industrial pollution.
Reformers argued that the country's political environment discouraged open debate.
Growing up in a stable environment can significantly affect a child's development.

items.definition: To set up or create an organization, system, or relationship on a firm basis, or to show something to be true through evidence.
exampleSentences: The United Nations was established in 1945 to promote international cooperation.
The inquiry sought to establish who was responsible for the policy failure.
Diplomatic relations between the two countries were established after decades of hostility.

items.definition: A topic or problem that people discuss or that requires a decision, or to formally publish, provide, or make something available, especially by an official body.
exampleSentences: Immigration remains one of the most divisive issues in the upcoming election.
The government issued a decree banning public gatherings during the crisis.
Local authorities issue permits for any construction within the historic district.
items.translationTR: konu, sorun; (fiil) yayımlamak, resmi olarak vermek (belge/karar)

items.definition: Relating to, based on, or permitted by the law.
exampleSentences: The company took legal action against the supplier for breach of contract.
Same-sex marriage became legal in the country after a landmark court ruling.
Citizens have the legal right to appeal decisions made by local government.

items.definition: To make or pass laws, especially by a governing body, or to make provision for a particular situation through law.
exampleSentences: Parliament voted to legislate against discrimination in the workplace.
It is difficult to legislate for every possible circumstance that may arise.
Several states have legislated to raise the minimum wage this year.

items.definition: A fundamental rule, belief, or truth that guides behaviour, reasoning, or the design of a system.
exampleSentences: The constitution is founded on the principle of equality before the law.
In principle, the new policy should reduce bureaucracy, though implementation may prove difficult.
She resigned rather than compromise her principles.

items.definition: To continue or go ahead with a course of action, especially after a pause or approval, or, in law, to bring a case against someone.
exampleSentences: The council decided to proceed with the redevelopment plan despite local opposition.
Once the warrant was issued, police were authorized to proceed with the arrest.
The prosecution proceeded against the former official on charges of corruption.
items.translationTR: devam etmek, ilerlemek; (hukuk) dava açmak, kovuşturmaya geçmek

items.definition: To need something for a particular purpose, or to officially demand that someone do something, especially under a rule or law.
exampleSentences: The new legislation requires companies to disclose their carbon emissions annually.
Obtaining a visa requires submitting several supporting documents.
The court required the defendant to pay damages to the victim.
items.translationTR: gerektirmek; (resmi olarak) zorunlu kılmak, talep etmek

items.definition: The particular function, position, or part that a person or institution has within a society, organization, or situation.
exampleSentences: Civil society organizations play a crucial role in holding governments accountable.
The committee's role is to advise ministers on proposed legislation.
She took on a leading role in the campaign for judicial reform.

items.definition: Important, noteworthy, or large enough to have a meaningful effect.
exampleSentences: The new regulations represent a significant shift in environmental policy.
There has been a significant increase in voter turnout since the reform.
Community leaders played a significant part in resolving the dispute.

items.definition: A single person considered separately from a group, or, as an adjective, relating to, characteristic of, or intended for one particular person rather than a group.
exampleSentences: The law protects the rights of the individual against arbitrary state action.
Each individual case is reviewed on its own merits by the tribunal.
The policy allows for individual exemptions in cases of genuine hardship.

items.definition: To include or affect something as a necessary part or consequence, or to cause someone to take part in an activity.
exampleSentences: Reforming the pension system will inevitably involve difficult political trade-offs.
The scandal involved several senior members of the government.
Community leaders were involved in drafting the new housing policy.

items.definition: A group of people living in the same area, or sharing common characteristics, interests, or nationality within a wider society.
exampleSentences: The new policy was developed in close consultation with the local community.
Ethnic and religious communities have long coexisted in the region.
International community leaders condemned the coup within hours.

items.definition: The customs, beliefs, values, and social behaviour of a particular society or group, or the shared attitudes characteristic of an organization.
exampleSentences: The reforms aim to change the culture of impunity within the police force.
Immigration has enriched the country's culture over successive generations.
Building a culture of transparency in government requires more than new laws.

items.definition: An organization founded for a particular purpose, especially research, education, or policy, or, as a verb, to introduce or establish a policy, practice, or legal proceeding.
exampleSentences: The research institute published a report on rising inequality.
The government instituted a curfew following the outbreak of unrest.
New safety regulations were instituted after the factory disaster.

items.definition: To take part in or become actively involved in an activity or event.
exampleSentences: Citizens were encouraged to participate in the public consultation on the new bylaw.
Only a fraction of eligible voters participated in the referendum.
NGOs were invited to participate in drafting the human rights legislation.

items.definition: Capable of happening, developing, or being used in the future, or, as a noun, the capacity for such future development.
exampleSentences: The reform has the potential to reduce corruption significantly if properly enforced.
Officials flagged the bill as a potential threat to civil liberties.
Investment in education is essential to unlocking the region's economic potential.

items.definition: Coming or existing before something else in time or order.
exampleSentences: The new administration reversed several previous decisions on immigration policy.
Under the previous government, welfare spending was cut sharply.
There is no record of any previous conviction for the defendant.

items.definition: A particular area, especially one defined by geographic, administrative, or cultural boundaries, or, informally, an approximate amount.
exampleSentences: The conflict has displaced hundreds of thousands of people across the region.
Each region elects its own representatives to the national assembly.
The proposed budget is in the region of two billion lira.
items.translationTR: bölge; (deyim) 'in the region of' - yaklaşık olarak

items.definition: To control an activity, industry, or process by means of rules, especially those set by an official body.
exampleSentences: An independent commission was set up to regulate the banking sector.
The new law regulates the use of personal data by private companies.
Utilities are heavily regulated to protect consumers from unfair pricing.

items.definition: Closely connected or applicable to the matter at hand.
exampleSentences: The committee requested all documents relevant to the corruption investigation.
Community input is highly relevant when designing local housing policy.
The judge ruled that the earlier testimony was no longer relevant to the case.

items.definition: To limit or place controls on the extent, movement, or freedom of something or someone.
exampleSentences: The new curfew restricts residents' movement between midnight and dawn.
Several countries have restricted imports of the product on safety grounds.
Freedom of assembly was severely restricted under the previous regime.

items.definition: A long-established custom, belief, or practice passed down within a society or group.
exampleSentences: The village has a long tradition of resolving disputes through community elders.
Reformers argue that some legal traditions no longer serve modern society.
The ceremony draws on a centuries-old political tradition.

items.definition: To have an influence on someone or something, often producing a change; not to be confused with the noun 'effect,' meaning a result.
exampleSentences: The new tax bracket will affect middle-income households the most.
Prolonged drought has severely affected agricultural communities in the region.
Public opinion can affect how quickly lawmakers respond to a crisis.
items.translationTR: etkilemek (fiil) — isim olan 'effect' (sonuç, etki) ile karıştırılmamalı

items.definition: To cause physical harm to someone, or, in law, to cause harm or loss to a person's rights or interests, as in 'the injured party.'
exampleSentences: Several protesters were injured when police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.
The court awarded compensation to the injured party in the negligence case.
The new safety regulations aim to reduce the number of workers injured on construction sites.
items.translationTR: yaralamak; (hukuk) zarar vermek ('injured party' - zarar gören taraf)

items.definition: To live in a particular place on a permanent or long-term basis, or, formally, (of power, authority, or a quality) to be located in or belong to something.
exampleSentences: Thousands of refugees now reside in camps along the border.
Under the constitution, ultimate authority resides in the elected parliament.
Foreign nationals who reside in the country for over five years may apply for citizenship.
items.translationTR: ikamet etmek, oturmak; (yetki/güç için) -de bulunmak, ait olmak

items.definition: Following as a result or effect of something, especially a previous event or action.
exampleSentences: The consequent rise in unemployment put pressure on the welfare system.
Delays in the vote led to a consequent postponement of the reform's implementation.
Public distrust in institutions, and the consequent decline in voter turnout, worried policymakers.
